title: The PPT per-slide re-parse spans the PowerPoint Document stream the presentation already retains, and the glibc heap-trim artifact 0606 left open disappears
code_state: crates/litchi-ppt only; ten files; no public API signature, error type, limit or output byte changed; no new unsafe and no new dependency
reason_codes: change 0606's Limitations named this exact follow-on and attributed its +4.71% ppt_semantic_full_text regression to it; change 0630 carries it as queue item 16

SlideFactory::parse_slide_at_offset, NotesIndex::try_build_with_limits (a whole DocumentContainer re-parse) and SpeakerNotes::parse_with_limits all re-parsed the retained stream through the copying &[u8] entry point; all three now take a PayloadStore and borrow

the removed work is deterministic: 160 allocations and 160 memcpy calls per Presentation::slides() on 45543.ppt, 98 per speaker-notes read on headers_footers_2007.ppt, with the open path's counts bit-identical

the 1,000-iteration open+list-slides loop artifact 0606 characterized but did not eliminate is gone: 171,889 -> 667 minor faults and 1.524 G -> 552 M instructions under glibc defaults, and the after leg now lands on the same instruction count as a run with the thresholds pinned
value identity is proved by 0606's own 30-fixture reader-dump differential, which reproduces 0606's digest 9cdddef6e870aa35884738c3f1729c9e12b6ca7bc22b2e551a4dad586c236b7c on both legs

accepted_evidence.counts: callgrind isolation pairs, s=10 and s=110, differenced and divided by 100, per leg for eager-open, eager-slides, eager-text, eager-notes and owned-edit-save; whole-sample totals plus per-symbol self/inclusive Ir and memcpy/malloc/parse_impl call counts
accepted_evidence.allocations: the 0606 counting-allocator driver, one operation after one untimed warm-up, six modes over two fixtures, both legs
accepted_evidence.native_counts: perf stat instructions, cycles and minor-faults; a 1,000-iteration loop under glibc defaults, the same loop with MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_/MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_ pinned at 8 MiB, and -r 200 single-shot processes
accepted_evidence.timing: tools/perf-baseline --warmup 5 --samples 40 on CPU 10, order A1 B1 B2 A2 then AA1 AA2 for the A/A floor in the same window, over four registered selectors and both PPT corpora; plus the scratch driver's five whole operations on two real fixtures in both allocator configurations
accepted_evidence.differential_oracle: change 0606's driver oracle mode over all 30 .ppt fixtures, both readers' full semantic surface including speaker notes, 12 owned-editor targets and 6 source-backed-editor targets, plus a record census and FNV digest; 30 of 30 dumps identical after normalizing two per-process-randomized HashMap Debug renderings
accepted_evidence.unit_tests: crates/litchi-ppt/src/presentation/tests.rs: owned and shared factories compared over four real fixtures for records, offsets, note descriptors, text, shapes and speaker notes; the copy budget asserted to accept and refuse identically at and one byte below a slide's payload total; an in-place edit of a borrowed slide payload asserted not to reach the Arc'd stream or its siblings

accepted_costs.open_regression: the open path, which this change does not touch, moves +0.25% in callgrind Ir, +0.85% in a native 1,000-iteration loop with cycles -0.10%, and +0.61%/+0.81% in paired p50 against floors of 1.04%/0.26%; identical call and allocation counts make it inlining drift after parse_with_limits became a wrapper, and it was not chased
accepted_costs.full_text_residue: ppt_semantic_full_text recovers -3.29% of 0606's +4.71% against a 0.15% floor, leaving about +1% against 0606's absolute pre-change number; the stated cause, Record's extra 8 bytes and the payload tag test, is untouched
accepted_costs.selector_attribution: ppt_semantic_open improves 4.64% because that selector's untimed per-iteration verification runs a full slides()+shapes()+text(); the improvement is allocator state, not a faster open, and the record says so
accepted_costs.instruction_counts: instructions rank work, not latency; callgrind counts rep movsb per byte and runs SHA-256 in software; one deterministic run per leg
accepted_costs.arc_traffic: every borrowed payload clones an Arc, so the per-record atomic increment replaces a malloc plus memcpy; the trade is measured natively, not assumed

known_gaps.strict_entry_points: reject_macro_records and inspect_source_text_atom on the source-backed resolve, and four sites in the owned Snapshot editor, still copy through Record::parse_strict_with_limits/parse_strict; they are once-per-resolve rather than once-per-slide and were left alone
known_gaps.registered_corpora: the only registered PPT corpora are two synthetic packages of 7,680 and 40,960 bytes; every real-fixture number comes from a scratch driver retained in this packet
known_gaps.rss: retained-byte figures are counting-allocator live bytes, not RSS; no cold-cache, physical-device or RSS measurement was taken
known_gaps.notes_fixtures: only three fixtures in the corpus carry a speaker-notes page; the notes measurements use headers_footers_2007.ppt because 45543.ppt has none
known_gaps.record_size: 41246-1.ppt still shows that on a record-dense, payload-light file the remaining cost is the Record struct itself; no packing was attempted

withheld: any registered speedup, throughput, cold-cache, physical-I/O, RSS, concurrency-scaling, producer-corpus or cross-platform result
